page.layout: One printed page. Page number at top centre. Arabic verse set full width across the top, right-aligned, nine lines. Below it, one column of Latin prose, set as separate indented paragraphs. The catchword "quod" stands alone at the right, below the last line. No running head, no margin notes.

main_text.p: فما ذاك الا مثل خرقة حيضة [?] .
اذا لم يكن اقرار منك لسيدا [?] :
فلا يطغوك الظالمين بقولهم [?] . الى الله
فقد قال عزّ الله قولا [?] . ختم بـ [?]
يا ين خلاص الناس بالناس كايف [?] . فلا
Sine Confessione nulla est tua pœnitentia, nec tuum deletur crimen, etiamsi Martyr obieris.
Et quamuis totum ieiunaueris seculum continentia, & laboribus, ac utrumque iugiter flexeris genu.
Etiamsi elargita manus tua liberaliter fuerit in terra dando eius incolis obsequentibus, & inobedientibus.
Hoc nihil aliud erit, nisi instar panni menstruatæ, si præceptori confessus non fueris.
Nec te decipiant seductores dicendo: Deo Confessionem cfferre, est laudabile.
Iam enim conclusit Deus gloriosus dicto, quod

page.notes: The Arabic lines are very faint and the scan is low in resolution. I read the letters as far as I could, but many words, especially at line ends and in the last three lines, are doubtful and are marked [?]. The line "ختم بـ" is cut off at the edge of the printed block. The Latin is clear. "menstruatæ" is printed as such (probably for "menstruatæ"; left as printed). "cfferre" is printed as such (probably for "offerre"; left as printed). "seculum" and "ieiunaueris" are as printed. The word "quod" at the foot is the catchword and is not repeated in the text.
